A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Block Linearization work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–I are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original reasoning accuracy, inference speed, calibration runtime, perplexity, and ablation results across several language models.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, RULER evaluations, and further layer-selection experiments.

M1.justification: The LMMSE weight/bias estimator, CCA-bound layer ranking, substitution procedure, and residual handling remain unchanged in Algorithms 1–2. The added selection-criterion experiments test alternatives without changing the proposed NBL procedure.

E1.justification: Appendices F.3–F.4 add RULER attention-intensive reasoning and dependency-tracking evaluations on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and Llama-3.1-8B. This substantially extends task coverage: v1 examined context-length effects on speed but did not evaluate accuracy on this attention-dependent benchmark. Existing datasets and tasks remain represented.

E2.justification: PruneNet is newly evaluated in Tables 2–4. The existing DeepSeek comparison additionally gains SliceGPT and SLEB, while the quantized 70B comparison gains SLEB in Table 5. Appendix C.1 also introduces direct-NMSE layer selection as a comparator.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce RULER evaluation at 4K context length with two to four attention-layer substitutions and direct-NMSE selection of 12 Mistral layers. Tables 2–5 add sparsity reporting excluding embedding/projection layers, and the new PruneNet evaluation uses a tuned learning rate. Existing benchmark shot counts, calibration settings, and speed-measurement procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds the direct-NMSE versus CCA-bound ablation, tests attention-dependent performance on RULER, and compares CCA versus cosine selection on RULER for two models. Greedy-selection analysis expands from Mistral to Llama-3.1-8B. These materially strengthen tests of the method's selection mechanism and contextual robustness.

E5.justification: V2 first supplies uncertainty intervals for existing cosine-selection and Mistral greedy-selection averages in Tables 17–18 and 21. The pooled-standard-error approach and existing accuracy/speed uncertainty tables are retained. No additional seed or repeated-run counts are reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the added comparisons and analyses. Appendix C.1 reports 68.3% accuracy with CCA selection versus 39.1% with direct NMSE; RULER Table 16 reports 86.19% for NBL-4 versus 83.15% for DROP-4. Previously shared benchmark scores largely remain unchanged. V1 Table 8's per-task DeepSeek four-layer results disappear, although their aggregate accuracy and speed results remain in v2 Table 10.

T1.justification: The main LMMSE proposition, CCA error bound, and proofs are retained. Appendix F.4 adds an explicit rotation counterexample demonstrating perfect linear predictability despite zero corresponding-vector cosine similarity. New Appendix C.1 also introduces a normalization ambiguity by equating output second moment with covariance trace without stating a centering assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free LMMSE substitution, CCA-guided error control, and improved inference efficiency with competitive reasoning accuracy. The headline DeepSeek speed/accuracy claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands the rationale for CCA through variance weighting, whitening, and structural alignment, and distinguishes sparsity tradeoffs from throughput tradeoffs. New Section 6 goes beyond retained Appendix I by discussing history-agnostic behavior under indiscriminate linearization and possible hallucination-like effects under calibration mismatch, alongside more specific future remedies.

D1.justification: The abstract newly provides an NBL implementation repository link. Section 4 documents learning-rate tuning for the newly evaluated PruneNet baseline, from its stated default of 5e-4 to 1e-4. Existing NBL implementation, hardware, calibration, LoRA, and quantization details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to PruneNet, RULER, and Hardoon et al.'s CCA survey, supporting the new comparisons and selection rationale. The broader research positioning remains stable; publication updates for works such as LoLCATs and LoftQ represent the same previously cited research.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. Changes include localized rewriting, corrected activation-matrix orientation notation, a new discussion section, and reorganization of Appendix E, including moving speculative decoding. The title-page correspondence and publication information also change.

P2.justification: The principal comparison tables gain sparsity columns and expanded baseline blocks, especially the DeepSeek table. V2 adds RULER, direct-NMSE, and Llama greedy-selection tables, revises ablation headings and uncertainty displays, and partly incorporates the former DeepSeek appendix table into Table 4. These substantially expand the result displays, while the four existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves empirical scrutiny through attention-dependent RULER tests, a direct-NMSE control, and broader baseline comparisons. Added uncertainty reporting, implementation access information, and specific limitations also improve transparency. The gain is qualified: RULER evidence covers only 4K contexts and small substitution counts, some DeepSeek per-task detail is removed, and Appendix C.1 introduces an unstated centering assumption. These changes provide a useful but limited net improvement over v1's already substantial evaluation.
